bull.b: A $2B strategic equity infusion and multiyear supply agreement with NVIDIA materially strengthens liquidity and ties demand to a large, creditworthy customer. This reduces funding risk for capacity expansion, secures multi-year revenue visibility and supports longer-term project economics and supply commitments.

A record backlog with orders into 2028 gives durable revenue visibility that supports capital allocation and production planning. Multi-year LTAs smooth demand cyclicality, improve forecasting for capacity ramps, and increase the probability that fixed-cost absorption will sustain margin expansion over multiple years.

Doubling (and then >2x again) indium phosphide capacity with better 6-inch yields creates a structural manufacturing advantage in constrained markets. Higher wafer-scale yields and internal capacity reduce per-unit costs, ease supply bottlenecks, and enable scale into large datacenter and CPO opportunities over the next 2+ years.

bear.b: A sharp swing to negative trailing‑12‑month free cash flow and weak cash conversion undermines earnings quality and raises funding risk for aggressive capex and R&D plans. Persistent cash deficits would force tradeoffs in investment pace or require external financing, stressing long‑term capital allocation.

bear.t: Execution and qualification risk on new ramps
bear.b: New-product and multi-site scale-ups require customer qualification, pilot-to-volume transitions and supply-chain coordination. Delays or yield setbacks can defer revenue realization, compress expected margin benefits, and extend the period before investments reach profitable scale, raising structural execution risk.

Sustained higher R&D intensity and elevated capex to fund rapid capacity expansion will pressure near-term operating leverage and free cash flow until new volumes scale. If revenue ramps miss targets, persistent elevated spend can compress margins and weaken balance-sheet flexibility.
